purpose: The evidence reports that the campaign family in docs/findings/2026-10-02-m16-a-fu2-rally-review-snapshot.json does not cover must name the implementer and the reviewer that actually ran, including whether the reviewer's context was fresh (docs/contracts/CLI-EVIDENCE.md, 'Evidence record minimum'; owner ruling 2026-09-28). Rally is not reachable from CI or from an offline check, so the review facts read out of the Rally activity log are committed here and enforced against the reports and against the harness that writes them by tools/tests/test_evidence_review_identity.py.
source: Rally activity log of project crimson-skies, read with the `rally` MCP server (get_task history per task) on 2026-10-02T04:00Z by bunny-2/bunny-2, agent instance acting under M16-A-FU4 (#483).
claim_started_source: Rally's `task.started` event, or its `task.resumed` event where another agent's implement lease had expired and a different agent picked the stage up (F02-C, F10-D).
actor_meaning: Rally actor strings are `<agent instance>/<session label>`. Two claims from the same actor string are the same agent instance, so the second is not independent of the first (owner ruling 2026-09-28, review policy).
independent_is_derived: The check derives independence from actor equality; this file records the actors and the event timestamps, not a verdict.
every_merged_stage_has_a_review_claim: Rally only merges a stage through complete_review or its landing queue, so every stage listed here has at least one review claim and a reviewer to name.
scope: Only the stages whose committed `review.identity` was still a hand-over placeholder when this file was written. Every other committed report is either already honest or names no reviewer at all without carrying a placeholder; the latter are filed as follow-up #484 rather than rewritten here. F14-D.7 was added to this file later, under F14-D.7-SNAPSHOT (#578): its report already named the implementer and the reviewer honestly but was written before any snapshot covered it, so the snapshot-backed rules were not enforced for it; see `entries_added_after_writing`.
actor_spelling: The check matches the recorded `actor` verbatim against the committed report's `review.identity`, so `actor` holds the spelling the report itself uses. Every entry this file's author wrote spells Rally's `<agent instance>/<session label>` actor string out in its report, so there `actor` is that whole string. F14-D.7's report spells the agent as `openrouter/stealth-space-bunny-alpha (bunny-alpha-2, ...)`, so its `actor` is the agent-instance name `bunny-alpha-2` and its `rally_actor` holds Rally's verbatim actor string. Both spellings name the same instance and the same session, and nothing else in the check reads the spelling: the equality that derives independence compares the two recorded actors, so it is unaffected.
report_written_by_meaning: Derived from the report's own `created_at` against the claim windows in the Rally log: a `created_at` inside a review claim means the reviewer regenerated the report, one inside the implement claim means the committed copy is the implementer's. `report_regenerated_on_reviewed_commit` is `true` only when the reviewer's run wrote the copy that reached `main`.

entries_added_after_writing.note: The review of #490 was done by the same agent instance that implemented it and the branch landed through Rally's landing queue, so its `task.merged` event is a system event rather than a reviewer action. The entry was therefore added only after that event really existed (2026-10-03T08:47:46Z); the reviewer of #490 declined to predict one. Read with the `rally` MCP server (get_activity for #490) from the activity log, not from the hand-over summaries.

earlier_review_claims.outcome: the implementer's own review lease expired on 2026-09-24T00:38:35Z without merging anything; it recorded no finding and the stage was reviewed again from scratch

earlier_implement_claims.outcome: the implement lease expired on 2026-09-24T03:50:01Z; devin-1 resumed the same branch and submitted it
the implement lease expired on 2026-09-29T22:58:01Z; mimo-1 resumed the stage and rebuilt it from origin/main because the branch was never pushed

tasks.self_review: The implementer and the reviewer are the same agent instance and model, so this review is not independent evidence and the check requires the report to keep saying so; the reviewer of #490 recorded the same in its `complete_review` notes.
tasks.notes: `merge_event` is a system event: the reviewer approved the stage at `approval_event` and Rally's landing queue rebased the branch onto main and fast-forwarded main to `merged_sha`, so the copy of the report on main is the one the reviewer's own run wrote (`created_at` 2026-10-03T08:32:27Z, inside the review claim). See `actor_spelling` for why `actor` is the agent-instance name rather than Rally's `<instance>/<session>` string.
